$comment: Full evaluation campaign — every pillar from the dissertation evaluation plan.
Designed for HPC: each task runs independently under SLURM array; aggregator combines.
All baseline / variant / ablation experiments use simbench_lv_constrained_45 so the slack
budget is tight enough that variant outcomes are actually distinguishable.  Cascading,
scaling, cold-day stress and generator-failure experiments live in their own sections.
Reconfiguration uses simbench_lv_reconfig (same grid + 5 backup branches per sector).
name: eval_full

experiments.$comment: Pillar 1 — Functional restoration quality.  Three slack budgets show the curve from easy (80 %) to hard (30 %).
experiments.name: functional_baseline

experiments.$comment: Pillar 2 — Optimality gap.  Pairs every scare run with an oracle on the same (grid, seed).
experiments.name: optimality_gap

experiments.$comment: Strawman comparison — single-level (gossip only) vs full architecture.
experiments.name: variant_comparison

experiments.$comment: Pillar 4 — ablation matrix.  One ablation per architectural component.
experiments.name: ablation

experiments.$comment: Cold-day thermal stress.  Heat loads scaled 1.5×, slack supply temperature dropped to 70 °C — narrows the headroom against the 60 °C lower bound so the heat sector actually exercises gossip + curtailment.
experiments.name: cold_day_stress

experiments.$comment: Generator-class failures.  Compares branch-only vs generator-only vs mixed contingency types — generator failures are arguably more realistic for restoration (a CHP trips, not a line) and exercise different sectors.
experiments.name: generator_failure

$comment: Pillar 7 — Scaling.  Three simbench LV variants spanning roughly a decade of node count:
small  ≈   36 nodes (1-LV-rural1)
medium ≈  137 nodes (1-LV-semiurb4)
large  ≈  396 nodes (1-LV-rural3, the established benchmark)
All run with the same 50 % slack budget so the only varying axis is grid size.
n_seeds smaller than the baselines because the per-task wallclock on the large grid is the bottleneck.
experiments.name: scaling

$comment: Pillar 8 — Reconfiguration.  Uses simbench_lv_reconfig: the constrained LV grid
augmented with 5 normally-open backup branches per sector (15 total) placed via
add_backup_lines so the GridReconfigurator's path search has alternative routes
to discover when a primary line trips.  Failures bias toward branches because the
reconfiguration pathway only fires on BranchFailureEvent; generator failures don't
test reconfiguration.
experiments.name: reconfiguration
